It never stops or touches a kcp, kine or OpenBao it did not start. It asks the kernel for three free 127.0.0.1 ports, for kcp, kine and OpenBao, instead of pinning any, so it cannot collide with another instance on the machine. It starts kcp with ROOT=$ACCEPT_ROOT/kcp and KCP_SECURE_PORT and KINE_ENDPOINT set to two of those ports through deploy/start-kcp.sh; installs the provider with KUBECONFIG_PATH=$ACCEPT_ROOT/kcp/admin.kubeconfig through deploy/install-provider.sh; builds ./cmd/deno-kcp-provider into $ACCEPT_ROOT; starts OpenBao with OPENBAO_DIR=$ACCEPT_ROOT/openbao and OPENBAO_LISTEN on the third port through deploy/start-openbao.sh; and runs the provider with --kubeconfig, --openbao-addr http://<openbao port>, --openbao-token root and RUNS_DIR=$ACCEPT_ROOT/runs. It then runs deploy/examples/atproto/market/apply.sh with ORG_ROOT the repository parent, KUBECONFIG the kcp admin kubeconfig, OPENBAO_LISTEN the same address, START_OPENBAO=0, a bounded WAIT_SECONDS, and KEY_FILE, BOB_KEY_FILE and BIDDER_KEY_FILE under $ACCEPT_ROOT. When apply.sh returns, whether it succeeded or not, accept.sh reads every DenoPod from kcp with kubectl and prints one line per check, each with its result and the decisive evidence: apply.sh exited 0; DenoPod plc in root:global, relay in root:relay, pds in root:alice, pds in root:bob and bidder in root:bob each reached phase Running and report ready true; DenoPod verifier in root:alice reached the terminal phase Succeeded; bob pds answers on its own name, which the provider proves with its readiness probe through the shim (kcpdns pds.default.bob.svc.kcp.local /xrpc/_health) and the host proves by fetching the same path from outside with curl https://127.0.0.1:2585/xrpc/_health; the bidder answers on bidder.default.bob.svc.kcp.local /oauth-client-metadata.json and on https://127.0.0.1:2586/oauth-client-metadata.json. Both host checks use https, because every service pod sets SERVICE_TLS true and the provider issues it a leaf, so the listener the host reaches is the TLS one; an http:// fetch of a TLS listener is not a check of anything and must not be written. http_code reports the status curl printed, and prints 000 exactly once when the fetch failed rather than appending a second fallback. And the five long-running pods are still Running with ready true when they are read a second time at least ten seconds later, so a pod that dies after startup fails the run. It prints a final table naming every check and its result, prints the tail of the provider log and the status of the failing pod when a check fails, and exits 0 only when every check passed.

intent: This context exists to specify the vendored OpenBao Kubernetes credential backend as it stands in third_party: how the credential backend is constructed and registered, how its config, login and role paths are served, how service account JWTs are reviewed against the Kubernetes TokenReview API, how the local service account token and CA certificate are cached between re-reads, how role namespace constraints are validated, and how the OpenBao CLI authenticates with this method. intent: This context exists to fix the contract of the audit package as a stable boundary between audit device backends and the rest of the server: a device supplies a Backend and a Formatter, the formatter serialises requests and responses into an AuditFormatWriter, and the hashing layer guarantees that secrets, tokens and potentially sensitive values are salted or HMAC'd before they leave the process. It is written so that the formatting and hashing behaviour cannot drift silently, because audit output is the forensic record and a leak or an unverifiable field is unrecoverable. The exported names, signatures and the required test files below are the parts that other packages and downstream devices depend on.

intent: This context exists to give the repository's integration tests and developers a runnable OpenBao server without an external install. The `test/integration` helpers build this package (see `baoembedBinary`, which runs `go build -o bin ./cmd/baoembed` with its working directory at `internal/baoembed`) and start it with `startProcess`, which launches the binary with stdout and stderr redirected into a log file and a new process group. Because the tests need to know when the server is up and, under TLS, which CA to trust, the command's contract is its readiness line: everything here is shaped around emitting `BAOEMBED <url>` (with the CA path when TLS is on) only after the embedded server accepts connections, and around accepting its configuration from flags with environment fallbacks so a test can drive it either way.
